Hi Emily — thanks for the heads up and the traces. We’re investigating now.

Short summary of what we’re looking at: around 08:40 PT the controller triggered an automatic prefetch rebalancing job in the us-west prefetch layer to redistribute cached prefixes across nodes following a background slot reassignment. The rebalancer should be background-friendly, but preliminary telemetry shows the rebalancing coincided with increased queue depth on several prefetch workers which could explain the P95 bump.

We’ll confirm scope quickly and follow up with an ETA for mitigation. I’m looping in Marissa (Customer Ops) and Ben (Runtime).

-Jonas

Quick ops update — reproduced in staging: when the controller starts a prefetch rebalancing wave under nonzero incoming traffic, prefetch workers perform synchronized metadata fetches that slightly block token-serving threads and increase per-request tail latency. We have a mitigation path: throttle rebalancer concurrency and stagger worker heartbeats; that should bring p95 back to baseline within ~30 minutes after we roll the change to us-west.

I’m attaching a compact log snippet and a snapshot of the prefetch queue lengths at the time-of-spike. I’ll open a Jira (INFR-8721) for the mitigation + a small runtime fix to make rebalancing backpressure-aware.

Subject: Customer notification: transient P95 increase in us-west — we're on it

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for flagging this. We investigated and identified a coordinated prefetch rebalancing job in the us-west prefetch tier that overlapped with production traffic and increased queue depth on a subset of workers.

What we did so far (11:00 PT):
- Throttled the rebalancer and staggered worker heartbeats to reduce metadata-fanout during active traffic (applied to us-west).
- Enabled an emergency backpressure limit for prefetch threads to prevent future synchronized stalls.

Customer impact: transient P95 latency increase (approx. 95th percentile latency rose ~2x for ~35 minutes starting ~08:45 PT). A small number of requests hit transient 504s during the same window; overall success rate remained >99.6%.

Next steps / ETA:
- Short-term mitigation is live in us-west; we expect p95 to return to baseline within 30 minutes and will monitor for two hours.
- Engineering will follow with a targeted runtime change (INFR-8721) to make rebalancing backpressure-aware and to add a canary-run mode to diminish impact on production traffic. Target: completed staging validation by 2026-03-24.
- We'll post a summarized advisory on our Statuspage and follow up with a post-incident note once the Jira is complete.

We’ll keep you updated here and on the statuspage link below. Apologies for the disruption — please reach out if you want a dedicated bridge.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: brief RCA & follow-ups for Solstice Digital (prefetch rebalancing)

Team — finalizing a short RCA for Solstice and for the public postmortem. Draft notes below (for inclusion on statuspage and customer follow-up):

Timeline:
- 08:40 PT — controller initiated prefetch rebalancing in us-west (routine slot reassignment).
- 08:45–09:20 PT — prefetch queue depth elevated on ~18% of workers; synchronized metadata refresh caused token-serving contention; observed P95 increase ~2x and a handful of 504s.
- 09:00 PT — automated health checks flagged p95 deviation; Pager not fired (below pager threshold) but Ops was alerted via telemetry.
- 10:50 PT — mitigation (throttle + stagger heartbeats) rolled; 11:05 PT — p95 returned to baseline.

Root cause: controller rebalancer did not respect concurrent traffic levels and performed metadata fetches in a way that allowed synchronization across prefetch workers, which amplified queueing under load.

Corrective actions (short-term):
- Keep throttle + staggered heartbeats in us-west for 72 hours.
- Add an automated guardrail: rebalancer must enter 'safe mode' if p95 exceeds 1.5x baseline.

Corrective actions (long-term):
- Engineering (Ben) will implement INFR-8721 to make rebalancer backpressure-aware and introduce canary-mode. Target: PR by 2026-03-26, staging validation by 2026-03-24.
- Post-incident: publish a public postmortem on status.redwood.inference and notify customers who observed impact with the timeline and files attached.

Customer comms plan: Marissa to post the statuspage advisory, and send an email to affected customers with timeline, attachments (logs & snapshot), and planned mitigations. Jonas to prepare a short technical appendix for the postmortem.

Laura — can you confirm if any larger SLAs were impacted for Solstice? If so, escalate to Sales for credit discussion.

Thanks — Jonas
